sections.title: Fast Food and a Healthy Diet
sections.instr: Read the text. Fill in each gap with ONE word. You must use a word which is somewhere in the rest of the text.

blocks.x: Fast Food and a Healthy Diet

Fast food is very popular all over the world. It is prepared quickly, it is usually cheap, and it can be eaten almost anywhere. In many countries, fast food restaurants can be found on almost every street, and they are especially {{1}} with students and people who have little time to cook.

However, while people continue to buy fast {{2}}, doctors remind us that eating a balanced diet is important for good health. A balanced diet, which includes fruit, vegetables, grains and enough water, plays an important role in protecting our {{3}}.

In recent years, many fast food {{4}} have started to offer healthier options, such as salads, grilled dishes and fresh juice. These healthier {{5}} allow people to enjoy convenient meals without always choosing something unhealthy.

Experts agree that fast food does not have to disappear from our lives completely. Balance is the key to healthy eating. Maintaining a {{6}} between fast food and nutritious home-cooked meals is essential for a healthy lifestyle.

after.x: Fast food va sog‘lom ovqatlanish — tarjima

Tez tayyorlanadigan taomlar (fast food) butun dunyoda juda mashhur. Ular tez tayyorlanadi, odatda arzon bo'ladi va deyarli istalgan joyda yeyish mumkin. Ko'plab mamlakatlarda fast food restoranlarini deyarli har bir ko'chada uchratish mumkin va ular ayniqsa talabalar hamda ovqat pishirishga vaqti kam odamlar orasida mashhur (popular).

Biroq odamlar fast food (food) sotib olishda davom etayotgan bir paytda, shifokorlar muvozanatli ovqatlanish yaxshi sog'liq uchun muhim ekanini eslatib turishadi. Meva, sabzavot, don mahsulotlari va yetarli miqdorda suvni o'z ichiga olgan muvozanatli ovqatlanish sog'lig'imizni (health) himoya qilishda muhim rol o'ynaydi.

So'nggi yillarda ko'plab fast food restoranlari (restaurants) salatlar, grilda pishirilgan taomlar va yangi siqilgan sharbat kabi sog'lomroq variantlarni taklif qila boshladi. Bu sog'lomroq variantlar (options) odamlarga har doim ham zararli narsani tanlamasdan, qulay taomlardan bahramand bo'lish imkonini beradi.

Mutaxassislar fast food hayotimizdan butunlay yo'qolib ketishi shart emasligiga qo'shilishadi. Muvozanat sog'lom ovqatlanishning kalitidir. Fast food va uyda tayyorlangan to'yimli taomlar o'rtasida muvozanatni (balance) saqlash sog'lom turmush tarzi uchun juda muhim.

sections.label: Part 2
sections.title: Summer tips
sections.instr: Read the texts 7–14 and the statements A–J. Decide which text matches with the situation described in the statements. Each statement can be used ONCE only. There are TWO extra statements which you do not need to use.

side.title: Statements
items: Get ready for the first day of school
Take part in a summer reading activity
Try a new sport by the sea
Put all your summer memories together
Discover something new near your home
Find a part-time job for the holidays

blocks.title: Text 7
blocks.x: If you enjoy photography, set your alarm a little earlier than usual. In the first hour after sunrise, the light is soft and warm, the streets are almost empty and the grass in the parks is still covered in dew, so even a simple phone camera can produce beautiful pictures. Try visiting the same place on several different days and compare how it looks.

blocks.title: Text 8
blocks.x: Instead of spending long afternoons at home sending messages to each other, why not arrange to see your friends in the local park? A picnic, a game of frisbee or simply sitting under the trees and chatting can turn an ordinary day into a special one. You do not need to be good at sport to join in; the point is simply to spend time together in the fresh air.

blocks.title: Text 9
blocks.x: Many public libraries organise a special challenge during the holidays, in which young people try to finish a certain number of books before September and receive a small prize at the end. Choose stories you would not normally pick up, from adventure novels to biographies of famous people, and write down the title of every book you complete.

blocks.title: Text 10
blocks.x: You do not need to travel abroad to have an adventure. Look at a map of your own town and find a museum, a garden or a walking path that you have never visited before. Many people live for years just a short bus ride away from interesting places they have never seen. Spend a day exploring them, and you may be surprised by what you find.

blocks.title: Text 11
blocks.x: Hot weather is a good reason to replace heavy snacks and sugary drinks with something lighter. Fruit, salads and plenty of water will help you stay full of energy during long, hot days. Summer markets are full of fresh local produce, so why not try a fruit or vegetable you have never tasted before and see how it compares with the crisps you usually buy?

blocks.title: Text 12
blocks.x: When the heat of the day has passed, there is no better time to be outside. Go for a slow walk, watch an open-air film or simply sit on a balcony and watch the sun go down. Because it stays light so late, there is plenty of time to relax after dinner, so make the most of it before the days begin to get shorter again.

blocks.title: Text 13
blocks.x: Tickets, postcards, photographs and little notes from your holidays are easy to lose. Before the summer ends, gather them all into a scrapbook or create a digital album, adding a few words about each day. In years to come, it will be a wonderful way to look back on everything you did and the people you met.

blocks.title: Text 14
blocks.x: During the last week of the holidays, start going to bed and getting up a little earlier, so that the first morning back is not a shock. Check that your bag, books and uniform are ready, and if you have saved some pocket money over the summer, use it to buy any new pens and notebooks that you will need.

Ko'plab ommaviy kutubxonalar ta'til davomida maxsus musobaqa tashkil qiladi: unda yoshlar sentyabrgacha ma'lum miqdordagi kitobni o'qib tugatishga harakat qilishadi va oxirida kichik sovg'a olishadi. Odatda qo'lingizga olmaydigan hikoyalarni, sarguzasht romanlaridan tortib mashhur odamlarning tarjimai holigacha tanlang va o'qib tugatgan har bir kitobingiz nomini yozib boring.
Text 10

Sarguzasht uchun chet elga borishingiz shart emas. O'z shahringiz xaritasiga qarang va ilgari hech qachon bormagan muzey, bog' yoki piyoda yo'lakni toping. Ko'p odamlar hech qachon ko'rmagan qiziqarli joylardan avtobusda bir necha bekat narida yillab yashashadi. Bir kunni ularni o'rganishga bag'ishlang va topganlaringizdan hayratda qolishingiz mumkin.
Text 11

Issiq havo og'ir gazaklar va shirin ichimliklarni yengilroq narsalar bilan almashtirish uchun yaxshi sabab. Mevalar, salatlar va ko'p suv uzun, issiq kunlarda kuch-quvvatga to'la bo'lishingizga yordam beradi. Yozgi bozorlar yangi mahalliy mahsulotlarga to'la, shunday ekan, nega ilgari hech qachon tatib ko'rmagan meva yoki sabzavotni sinab ko'rib, uni odatda sotib oladigan chipsingiz bilan solishtirmaysiz?
Text 12

Kunduzgi jazirama o'tib ketgach, tashqarida bo'lish uchun bundan yaxshiroq vaqt yo'q. Sekin sayr qiling, ochiq osmon ostida film tomosha qiling yoki shunchaki balkonda o'tirib, quyosh botishini kuzating. Kech soatlargacha yorug' bo'lgani uchun kechki ovqatdan keyin dam olishga ko'p vaqt bor, shuning uchun kunlar yana qisqara boshlashidan oldin undan maksimal foydalaning.
Text 13

Ta'tildagi chiptalar, otkritkalar, suratlar va kichik yozuvlar osongina yo'qolib qoladi. Yoz tugashidan oldin ularning hammasini skrapbuk (xotira albomi)ga to'plang yoki raqamli albom yarating va har bir kun haqida bir necha so'z qo'shing. Kelgusi yillarda bu qilgan barcha ishlaringiz va uchratgan odamlaringizni eslash uchun ajoyib usul bo'ladi.
Text 14

Ta'tilning oxirgi haftasida biroz ertaroq yotib, ertaroq tura boshlang, shunda maktabga qaytgan birinchi tong siz uchun zarba bo'lmaydi. Sumkangiz, kitoblaringiz va maktab formangiz tayyorligini tekshiring, agar yoz davomida biroz cho'ntak puli yig'gan bo'lsangiz, undan kerak bo'ladigan yangi ruchka va daftarlarni sotib olish uchun foydalaning.

blocks.x: From Waste Water to Drinking Water

blocks.title: Paragraph I
blocks.x: For decades, the city of Riverton relied on a single river and a group of underground wells for its drinking water, and its water authority drew up plans that were intended to meet the city's needs for the next fifty years. Those plans, however, did not anticipate how quickly circumstances would change. The population grew far faster than expected, several dry summers in a row left the river at record lows, and the wells began to fall as more water was pumped out than the rain could replace. The authority briefly considered building a plant to remove salt from seawater, but it concluded that such a solution would use too much energy. Instead, it turned to a more controversial idea: cleaning the city's used water so thoroughly that it could be drunk again.

blocks.title: Paragraph II
blocks.x: Turning waste water into drinking water is not a single process but a series of carefully designed steps. First, the water receives the same basic treatment as ordinary sewage, which removes solid material. It is then pushed through filters with holes so small that bacteria cannot pass through them. Next comes a process called reverse osmosis, in which the water is forced at high pressure through special membranes that hold back salts, medicines and other chemicals. Finally, it is exposed to powerful ultraviolet light, which destroys any remaining viruses.

blocks.title: Paragraph III
blocks.x: The authority planned to introduce the recycled water gradually, mixing it with river water before sending it into the city's pipes. Even this carefully prepared change, however, produced difficulties that had not been fully expected. Because the recycled water was so pure, it contained fewer of the natural minerals that people were used to, and some residents complained that it tasted flat. More seriously, engineers discovered that the new water reacted differently with the inside of some older pipes, and extra minerals had to be added to protect them.

blocks.title: Paragraph IV
blocks.x: The greatest obstacle, though, was not technical but psychological. When local newspapers began describing the project with the phrase from toilet to tap, many residents reacted with disgust, and a petition against the scheme was signed by several thousand people. Recognising that the project could not succeed without public support, the authority decided to move a significant part of its budget away from construction and into education. It opened a visitor centre where people could watch the treatment process, offered free tours to schools and published the results of every water test online.

blocks.title: Paragraph V
blocks.x: As the project developed, it began to attract attention far beyond the city. Water managers from neighbouring towns, which faced similar shortages, visited Riverton to study its methods, and several of them have since started building smaller plants of their own. Delegations have also arrived from countries in dry regions of the world, and the authority now runs regular training courses for engineers who hope to introduce similar systems at home.

blocks.title: Paragraph VI
blocks.x: Ten years after the first recycled water reached people's homes, surveys show that most residents are now comfortable drinking it. Officials believe that this change of attitude did not happen because of a single advertising campaign, but because of years of openness. By answering questions honestly, admitting problems when they occurred and allowing people to see the process for themselves, the authority slowly persuaded a sceptical public that the water was safe. Experts elsewhere warn that confidence of this kind cannot be bought quickly; it has to be built step by step.

after.x: Oqova suvdan ichimlik suvigacha — tarjima
Paragraph I

O'nlab yillar davomida Riverton shahri ichimlik suvi uchun bitta daryo va bir guruh yer osti quduqlariga tayangan, uning suv boshqarmasi esa shaharning keyingi ellik yillik ehtiyojlarini qondirishga mo'ljallangan rejalar tuzgan edi. Biroq bu rejalar sharoit qanchalik tez o'zgarishini oldindan ko'ra olmadi. Aholi kutilganidan ancha tez o'sdi, ketma-ket bir necha qurg'oqchil yoz daryo sathini rekord darajada pasaytirdi, quduqlarda esa yomg'ir to'ldira oladiganidan ko'proq suv tortib olingani sababli suv sathi tusha boshladi. Boshqarma qisqa muddat dengiz suvidan tuzni ajratib oladigan zavod qurishni ko'rib chiqdi, lekin bunday yechim juda ko'p energiya sarflaydi degan xulosaga keldi. Buning o'rniga u bahsliroq g'oyaga murojaat qildi: shaharning ishlatilgan suvini qayta ichish mumkin bo'ladigan darajada puxta tozalash.
Paragraph II

Oqova suvni ichimlik suviga aylantirish bitta jarayon emas, balki puxta ishlab chiqilgan bir qator bosqichlardir. Avval suv oddiy kanalizatsiya suvi kabi asosiy tozalovdan o'tadi va bunda qattiq moddalar olib tashlanadi. Keyin u teshiklari shunchalik kichikki, ulardan bakteriyalar o'ta olmaydigan filtrlar orqali o'tkaziladi. So'ng teskari osmos deb ataladigan jarayon keladi: unda suv yuqori bosim ostida tuzlar, dori-darmonlar va boshqa kimyoviy moddalarni ushlab qoladigan maxsus membranalardan o'tkaziladi. Nihoyat, u kuchli ultrabinafsha nurlar ta'siriga uchratiladi va bu qolgan har qanday virusni yo'q qiladi.
Paragraph III

Boshqarma qayta ishlangan suvni asta-sekin, shahar quvurlariga yuborishdan oldin daryo suvi bilan aralashtirib joriy etishni rejalashtirgan edi. Biroq hatto shunday puxta tayyorlangan o'zgarish ham to'liq kutilmagan qiyinchiliklarni keltirib chiqardi. Qayta ishlangan suv juda toza bo'lgani uchun unda odamlar o'rganib qolgan tabiiy minerallar kamroq edi va ba'zi aholi uning ta'mi bemaza ekanidan shikoyat qildi. Bundan jiddiyrog'i, muhandislar yangi suv ba'zi eski quvurlarning ichki yuzasi bilan boshqacha reaksiyaga kirishishini aniqlashdi va ularni himoya qilish uchun qo'shimcha minerallar qo'shishga to'g'ri keldi.
Paragraph IV

Biroq eng katta to'siq texnik emas, balki psixologik edi. Mahalliy gazetalar loyihani hojatxonadan jo'mrakka iborasi bilan tasvirlay boshlaganda, ko'plab aholi jirkanish bilan munosabat bildirdi va loyihaga qarshi petitsiyani bir necha ming kishi imzoladi. Loyiha jamoatchilik qo'llab-quvvatlovisiz muvaffaqiyatga erisha olmasligini anglagan boshqarma byudjetining katta qismini qurilishdan ta'limga o'tkazishga qaror qildi. U odamlar tozalash jarayonini kuzatishi mumkin bo'lgan tashrif markazini ochdi, maktablar uchun bepul ekskursiyalar taklif qildi va har bir suv tahlili natijalarini internetda e'lon qildi.
Paragraph V

Loyiha rivojlangani sari u shahardan ancha uzoqlarda ham e'tibor qozona boshladi. Shunga o'xshash suv tanqisligiga duch kelgan qo'shni shaharlarning suv boshqaruvchilari uning usullarini o'rganish uchun Rivertonga tashrif buyurishdi va ulardan bir nechtasi o'shandan beri o'zlarining kichikroq zavodlarini qura boshlagan. Dunyoning qurg'oqchil hududlaridagi mamlakatlardan ham delegatsiyalar kelgan va boshqarma endi o'z yurtlarida shunga o'xshash tizimlarni joriy qilmoqchi bo'lgan muhandislar uchun muntazam o'quv kurslari o'tkazadi.
Paragraph VI

Birinchi qayta ishlangan suv odamlarning uylariga yetib borganidan o'n yil o'tib, so'rovnomalar aholining ko'pchiligi endi uni bemalol ichayotganini ko'rsatmoqda. Rasmiylarning fikricha, munosabatdagi bu o'zgarish bitta reklama kampaniyasi tufayli emas, balki yillar davomidagi ochiqlik tufayli yuz bergan. Savollarga halol javob berish, muammolar yuzaga kelganda ularni tan olish va odamlarga jarayonni o'z ko'zi bilan ko'rish imkonini berish orqali boshqarma shubhali jamoatchilikni suv xavfsiz ekaniga asta-sekin ishontirdi. Boshqa joylardagi mutaxassislar bunday ishonchni tez sotib olib bo'lmasligi, uni qadam-baqadam qurish kerakligi haqida ogohlantirishadi.

blocks.x: Exploring the Deep Sea

The ocean covers around seventy percent of our planet, and most of it is very deep. Yet the deep sea remains one of the least explored places on Earth. Only about a quarter of the sea floor has been mapped in detail, and scientists actually possess more complete maps of the surface of the Moon than of the bottom of our own oceans. Today, a new generation of underwater robots is beginning to change this situation, while also raising important questions about how this fragile environment should be protected.

Exploring the deep sea is extremely difficult. Sunlight fades quickly as it passes through water, and below about one thousand metres there is no sunlight at all, so the deep ocean exists in permanent darkness. The water is close to freezing, and the pressure is enormous: at the bottom of the deepest ocean trenches, it is more than a thousand times greater than at the surface. For most of history, these conditions made the deep sea almost impossible for humans to reach.

Two types of robot have transformed deep-sea research. Remotely operated vehicles, or ROVs, are connected to a ship by a long cable and are controlled by pilots on board, who watch live video and use mechanical arms to collect samples. Autonomous underwater vehicles, or AUVs, have no cable; they follow a route programmed in advance and return with detailed images and measurements of the sea floor. The greatest advantage of both is that they allow scientists to explore the deepest parts of the ocean without putting human lives in danger, and they can remain underwater for many hours, or even days, at a time.

Robots have helped scientists to study some of the most surprising discoveries in the history of biology. In 1977, researchers exploring the Pacific Ocean found hot springs on the sea floor, known as hydrothermal vents, surrounded by crowds of living creatures. Until then, it had been widely believed that all life on Earth ultimately depended on energy from the sun. Around the vents, however, the food chain is based on bacteria that obtain energy from chemicals in the hot water. Giant tube worms, which can grow over two metres long, have no mouth or stomach; instead, they depend entirely on bacteria living inside their bodies, which turn these chemicals into energy.

The deep sea floor also contains valuable resources. In some regions, it is covered with potato-sized lumps known as nodules, which are rich in metals used to make batteries for electric cars and mobile phones. Several companies hope to collect them with huge machines. Scientists warn, however, that the nodules take millions of years to form, and that many deep-sea animals grow and reproduce very slowly. As a result, any damage caused by mining could last for an extremely long time. In one experiment carried out in 1989, researchers ploughed a small area of the sea floor; when they returned more than twenty-five years later, the tracks were still clearly visible and many species had not returned.

Responsibility for the sea floor beyond the waters of individual countries belongs to an international authority. So far, this body has granted licences that allow companies to explore large areas of the ocean, but it has not yet approved the rules that would allow commercial mining to begin, and it has not introduced a ban on mining. A growing number of governments, scientists and companies are now calling for a temporary pause until more is known about the risks.

Ironically, the same robots that make mining possible may also help to protect the deep sea. By mapping the sea floor, recording the animals that live there and monitoring changes over time, they can help scientists to identify the areas that are most valuable and most vulnerable. The challenge for the coming decades will be to ensure that exploration leads to understanding, rather than destruction.

Qizig'i shundaki, qazib olishni mumkin qilayotgan o'sha robotlarning o'zi dengiz tubini himoya qilishga ham yordam berishi mumkin. Dengiz tubini xaritaga tushirish, u yerda yashovchi hayvonlarni qayd etish va vaqt o'tishi bilan o'zgarishlarni kuzatish orqali ular olimlarga eng qimmatli va eng zaif hududlarni aniqlashda yordam bera oladi. blocks.x: The Cat That Hid in Plain Sight

Among the dense, mist-covered forests of the region lives a small spotted cat scarcely larger than a domestic one. For generations, it was regarded by scientists as merely a local population of a more widespread species, and it attracted little attention. In parts of its range, sightings were so rare that not a single confirmed record had been made during the whole of the preceding century, and some researchers privately suspected that the animal had already disappeared from those forests altogether.

Its rediscovery owed much to technology. Over the past two decades, camera traps, motion-activated cameras fixed to trees, have been placed along forest trails in growing numbers, and they began to record the elusive cat again and again. The images confirmed that the animal had survived, but they also raised a more intriguing question: was this cat really the same species as its relatives elsewhere, or something entirely distinct?

To answer it, researchers first compared the genetic material of cats from different regions and found that the forest population had evolved separately for a very long time. Genetic evidence alone, however, was not regarded as conclusive, since populations of the same species can differ considerably in their DNA. The team therefore also examined physical characteristics, comparing coat patterns and taking detailed measurements of the shape of each skull held in museum collections. Only when the genetic and physical evidence pointed in the same direction did they formally describe the cat as a separate species.

The circumstances of the cat's survival are now a source of growing concern. As forests are cleared, the remaining cats are increasingly forced into areas close to farms and towns, where they come into contact with domestic cats. Such encounters can transmit diseases to which the wild animals have little resistance, and the two may also interbreed, gradually eroding the genetic identity that makes the forest cat unique. Researchers regard this growing contact as the most serious problem facing the species.

It is by no means the only threat. Deforestation, the expansion of agriculture and mining have all reduced and divided the cat's habitat into ever smaller fragments. In recent years, fires, many of them started deliberately to clear land for cattle, have also become a major danger, spreading rapidly through forests weakened by drought and destroying in days areas that took centuries to grow.

The formal recognition of the species has had an unexpected consequence for the people who share its forests. Local communities had always had their own name for the animal, one that reflected its secretive habits. For some years after the scientific description, the local and the scientific names were used side by side; gradually, however, the formal name has taken the place of the local one in official reports, school books and conservation plans, a change that some anthropologists regard as a quiet loss of traditional knowledge.

Conservationists agree that protecting the cat will require more than legal recognition. Most argue that future efforts should combine long-term studies of the population, using camera traps and genetic sampling, with carefully managed public interest, such as small-scale wildlife tourism that brings income to local communities without disturbing the animals. Only by giving people a reason to value the forests, they suggest, can the cat's long-term survival be secured.

after.x: Ko‘z oldida yashiringan mushuk — tarjima

Mintaqaning zich, tuman bilan qoplangan o'rmonlari orasida uy mushugidan deyarli katta bo'lmagan kichik dog'li mushuk yashaydi. Avlodlar davomida olimlar uni shunchaki kengroq tarqalgan turning mahalliy populyatsiyasi deb hisoblashgan va u kam e'tibor qozongan. Uning tarqalish hududining ba'zi qismlarida u shunchalik kam ko'ringanki, oldingi butun asr davomida birorta ham tasdiqlangan qayd bo'lmagan va ba'zi tadqiqotchilar ichida bu hayvon o'sha o'rmonlardan allaqachon butunlay yo'qolib ketgan, deb gumon qilishgan.

Uning qayta kashf etilishi ko'p jihatdan texnologiyaga bog'liq bo'ldi. So'nggi yigirma yil ichida kamera tuzoqlari, ya'ni daraxtlarga o'rnatilgan, harakatga sezgir kameralar o'rmon so'qmoqlari bo'ylab tobora ko'proq joylashtirildi va ular bu qo'lga tushmas mushukni qayta-qayta qayd eta boshladi. Tasvirlar hayvon omon qolganini tasdiqladi, lekin ular yanada qiziqarliroq savolni ham tug'dirdi: bu mushuk haqiqatan ham boshqa joylardagi qarindoshlari bilan bir turmi yoki butunlay boshqa narsami?

Bunga javob berish uchun tadqiqotchilar avval turli hududlardagi mushuklarning genetik materialini solishtirishdi va o'rmon populyatsiyasi juda uzoq vaqt davomida alohida rivojlanganini aniqlashdi. Biroq faqat genetik dalil yakuniy deb hisoblanmadi, chunki bir turning populyatsiyalari DNK si bo'yicha sezilarli farq qilishi mumkin. Shuning uchun jamoa jismoniy xususiyatlarni ham o'rgandi: jun naqshlarini solishtirdi va muzey kolleksiyalarida saqlanayotgan har bir bosh suyagi shaklining batafsil o'lchovlarini oldi. Faqat genetik va jismoniy dalillar bir yo'nalishni ko'rsatgandagina ular mushukni rasman alohida tur sifatida ta'rifladilar.

Mushukning omon qolish sharoitlari endi tobora ortib borayotgan xavotir manbai. O'rmonlar kesilgani sari qolgan mushuklar tobora fermalar va shaharlarga yaqin hududlarga siqib chiqarilmoqda va u yerda uy mushuklari bilan aloqaga kirishmoqda. Bunday uchrashuvlar yovvoyi hayvonlarda kam qarshilik bo'lgan kasalliklarni yuqtirishi mumkin, ikkalasi o'zaro chatishishi ham mumkin va bu o'rmon mushugini noyob qiladigan genetik o'ziga xoslikni asta-sekin yemiradi. Tadqiqotchilar bu ortib borayotgan aloqani tur duch kelayotgan eng jiddiy muammo deb hisoblashadi.

Bu aslo yagona xavf emas. O'rmonlarning kesilishi, qishloq xo'jaligining kengayishi va kon qazish mushukning yashash muhitini qisqartirib, tobora kichikroq bo'laklarga bo'lib yuborgan. So'nggi yillarda yong'inlar ham katta xavfga aylandi, ularning ko'pchiligi qoramol uchun yer ochish maqsadida ataylab yoqilgan; ular qurg'oqchilik zaiflashtirgan o'rmonlar bo'ylab tez tarqalib, asrlar davomida o'sgan hududlarni bir necha kunda yo'q qilmoqda.

Turning rasman tan olinishi uning o'rmonlarida birga yashaydigan odamlar uchun kutilmagan oqibatga olib keldi. Mahalliy jamoalarning bu hayvon uchun doim o'z nomi bo'lgan va u hayvonning sirli odatlarini aks ettirgan. Ilmiy ta'rif berilganidan keyin bir necha yil davomida mahalliy va ilmiy nomlar yonma-yon ishlatilgan; biroq asta-sekin rasmiy nom rasmiy hisobotlarda, maktab kitoblarida va muhofaza rejalarida mahalliy nomning o'rnini egalladi. Ba'zi antropologlar bu o'zgarishni an'anaviy bilimning sezdirmay yo'qolishi deb hisoblashadi.

Tabiatni muhofaza qiluvchilar mushukni himoya qilish uchun huquqiy tan olishdan ko'proq narsa kerak bo'lishiga qo'shilishadi. Ularning ko'pchiligi kelajakdagi sa'y-harakatlar kamera tuzoqlari va genetik namunalar yordamida populyatsiyani uzoq muddat o'rganishni puxta boshqariladigan jamoatchilik qiziqishi bilan, masalan, hayvonlarni bezovta qilmasdan mahalliy jamoalarga daromad keltiradigan kichik hajmdagi yovvoyi tabiat turizmi bilan birlashtirishi kerakligini ta'kidlashadi. Ularning fikricha, faqat odamlarga o'rmonlarni qadrlash uchun sabab berish orqaligina mushukning uzoq muddatli omon qolishini ta'minlash mumkin.
